newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: UK multiples help Irish inflation meet EMU target.
newsitem.headline: UK multiples help Irish inflation meet EMU target.

text.p: Ireland's inflation inched up marginally in March but was below expectations and showed that Dublin should have no fear of missing Maastricht's EMU entry criteria on current trends, economists said on Thursday.
"It is a very good number indeed, very much better than expected. Looking at the components, overall the inflation outlook looks very good," NCB stockbrokers economist Eunan King told Reuters.

The March consumer price index published by the Central Statistics Office rose 0.1 percent on the month, up 0.2 percent for the four months from November and p 1.6 percent for 13 months from February last year.

One of the more surprising components in the CPI data was the low outturn for clothing and footwear which some economists argue may have benefitted from the influx of UK multiples into the Irish market keeping a competitive edge on prices.
McLaughlin said the figures were particularly interesting in that the Irish pound is down over 8.0 percentage points against sterling in the last six months.

"The big factor is that the areas in which one would expect the sterling influence to feed through, like clothing and footwear and durable household goods, you have seen very little inflationary pressure," McLaughlin said.
He said clothing and footwear were down 4.6 percent on a 13 month basis and durable household goods were only up 0.9 percent.
"I think it is competitive pressure, maybe the influence of some of the UK multiples which have moved into Ireland in the last year."

Britain's top food retailer Tesco joined a long line of UK multiples drawn by a "Celtic Tiger" economy, which is averaging a seven percent per annum growth rate, when it announced a 630 million pound ($973 million) takeover of Associated British Food Plc's Irish supermarket chains Quinnsworth and Crazy prices this month.
Debenhams, Boots and electrical giant Dixons are among British store groups that have recently opened outlets in Dublin, joining established retailers like Marks and Spencer, Next and Body Shop .
Partly thanks to the multiples Ireland looks set to comfortably undershoot Maastricht's EMU entry requirements.

"On these number I don't think there is any doubt that we will qualify on the Maastricht criteria," McLaughlin said, adding that the May figures will be critical to confirming the trend as they will provide an exact year-on-year comparisons.

The European Union harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP), which is used for intra-EU comparisons, showed no change for the month of March and was up 1.7 for the 13 months from February last year.
Recent data from Eurostat, the EU's statistical office, showed EU February inflation had slipped to 2.0 percent year-on-year, down from a 2.2 percent rise in the prior month.

Ten countries within the 15-nation bloc posted inflation figures under two percent, the office said. Economists are anticipating the Irish economy will post an annual inflation rate as low as 1.5 percent after today's data.
